name: CHAOS-3505 Go parity: StatusMapping loader + both normalizers
$limitation: Every mutation below is CLAUSE-level: it removes or inverts one conjunct, one comparison, one set member, or one ordering decision, never a whole function. Two things are deliberately NOT mutated here. (1) The DECLARED DIVERGENCE on LoadStatusMapping -- Python's source-relative DEFAULT_STATUS_MAPPING_PATH fallback has no Go equivalent, so there is no shared clause to mutate; it is covered by the written note on the function and by callers always supplying a path. (2) The `if typeRaw != ""` / `if statusRaw != ""` truthiness guards: normKey("") is "" and empty keys are never indexed, so removing the guard changes no observable result. Mutating it would report SURVIVED for a reason that is a property of the INDEX, not of the guard, so it is stated here instead of being listed as a fake kill.

mutations.rationale: _norm_key collapses INTERNAL whitespace runs, not just the ends. This is the exact shape a naive ToLower+TrimSpace port produces, and it silently stops 'In    Progress' from matching the indexed 'in progress'.
The case-folding clause, isolated from M1's whitespace clause. Jira's index holds 'bug'; a raw '  BUG  ' must still find it.

status_mapping.yaml:82 is `- type: bug` (with a space), which YAML parses as a MAPPING. Python indexes it under str(dict) == "{'type': 'bug'}". A mapping node's own .Value is empty, so this mutation drops the entry entirely -- the shape a port gets when it assumes every list item is a scalar.

Python's repr prefers SINGLE quotes. Double-quoting yields the key {"type": "bug"}, which differs from Python's {'type': 'bug'} by two bytes and matches nothing. Isolated from M3: the mapping is still walked and a key still produced.
Python's dict repr puts a SPACE after the colon. Dropping it is a one-byte divergence that no type checker sees, and it is not covered by M3 or M4 -- the quoting and the walk are both still correct.

THE ordering clause. Python iterates a dict in insertion (file) order and _index_values is last-wins, so a raw value listed under two categories resolves to the LATER one in the FILE. Sorting simulates exactly what a port that decoded YAML into a Go map suffers: quirks.yaml lists 'Shared Value' under todo then done, so file order resolves it to done while alphabetical order resolves it to todo.

First-wins instead of last-wins. Distinct from M6: the iteration ORDER is still correct here, only the overwrite rule flips. Both the cross-category collision and the provider-overrides-base pass depend on it.
`if not key: continue`. Without it an empty list entry indexes the empty string, which then makes an empty raw status match a category instead of falling through.

Base first, provider second -- that ordering is what makes a provider `statuses` entry an OVERRIDE. Swapping the two passes lets the shared base silently win, so jira's in_progress override of 'Shared Value' reverts to the base category.
`_as_status_category` returning None drops the whole category with no error. Accepting it instead indexes a bogus category name as if it were a real WorkItemStatusCategory.
The `_as_work_item_type` half of M10, on the shared single-section builder that serves status_labels, types and type_labels. A separate clause in a separate function: M10 cannot reach it.

QUIRK 7. Python reads the variable FIRST and lets it replace the caller's argument unconditionally. This mutation implements the SENSIBLE behaviour -- explicit argument wins -- which is precisely the bug-for-bug divergence D16 forbids.

CHAOS-3505, in the FIXING direction. The checked-in config has a linear section that the hardcoded tuple ignores, and this port mirrors that. Building the linear index is the eventual fix, and it must not be able to land silently inside a port whose contract is bug-for-bug parity.

QUIRK 8. typePriority omits the valid types 'pr' and 'merge_request', so a label matching ONLY one of them enters the label arm and then FALLS THROUGH to the type_raw arm. Returning early is what a port assuming the priority list is exhaustive would do, and it changes the answer from the type_raw arm's result to 'unknown'.

The priority ORDER itself, not its membership. Swapping the top two entries is invisible unless a case supplies both labels at once -- and it is the very inversion the Linear provider's hand-rolled _type_from_labels fallback already has in production (see the PR body's divergence table).
'Prefer more terminal states' is the documented rule for the status label arm. Reversing it makes an item labelled both todo and done report todo, understating completion in every rollup.

The default arm is `provider_key in {"github", "gitlab"}`. Dropping the gitlab disjunct sends every unmatched GitLab work item to 'unknown' instead of 'issue' -- one conjunct of a compound condition, which a whole-condition mutation could not distinguish.
One MEMBER of the closed-state set, not the whole set. A merged merge request would report 'unknown' while 'closed' still worked, so the existing Closed case cannot see this.
The GitLab spelling of the open state, isolated from GitHub's. Same shape as M18 on the other set.
